_comment: Bean sfhr. The three defects the bean names (70c7 empty body, 52dz folded title, nvbr blocked on a scrapped bean) plus the five the same readers found beside them, as they stood on 2026-09-20. sfhr is explicit that these are repaired BY THEIR OWNERS and that the bean does not edit them, so the check lists them and fails only on a NEW one. Remove an entry when its bean is repaired; check-bean-bodies reports an entry that no longer matches as stale, so the baseline shrinks rather than fossilises. 2026-09-21, bean sfhr again: the shadow-checklist reader added five more, each an OPEN bean whose canonical Done-when reads unticked while a copy below it reads ticked — 0hi8, 81t5, ivfw, jbx2, xgd8. Same rule: their owners repair them, the check fails only on a new one. b963 is NOT baselined: it had the same defect and it is this session's own bean, so it was ticked in place instead. 2026-09-21, second pass: the reader learned that a `---` horizontal rule ends the canonical section too — 61 beans use one where 141 use a heading, and it had been folding their later checklist back INTO the canonical section, blind to all 61 while reporting them clean. That found three more, all in this session's own epic: cvab and sfhr were repaired in place, and oh78 is baselined because it is queued next here and not yet claimed — repairing an unclaimed bean is the thing bean-coordination cautions against. oh78 was removed from the baseline the moment it was claimed and repaired in place — a baseline entry is a deferral, not a home. 2026-09-21, bean `sfhr`: the three shadow-checklist entries (0hi8, 81t5, xgd8) are REMOVED because they were repaired, not because they were tolerated. The check reported each as stale and failed until it shrank, which is what that rule looks like when it works. 0hi8's second section was a deliberate status report the canonical list never caught up with; 81t5 carried THREE checklists, the last of which declared itself the replacement; xgd8's revision sat 160 lines below the list every reader consults. In each the author's verdicts are unchanged -- only which list a reader finds first. 2026-09-22: ALL SIX dead-blocker entries removed because they were repaired, not tolerated — 1r0p, d5f1 and ktt2 (blocker `68dt`, completed), nvbr and rnfl (blocker `fsch`, scrapped), y1w9 (blocker `qif9`, completed). Each blocker's state was verified from the artefact rather than from its status word: `68dt` by schemas/python-deps.ts + requirements.txt + code-quality-gates.yml:148, `fsch` and `qif9` by their closing notes. Three of the six ALREADY carried a withdrawal later in the body while the original assertion stood unedited at the top — d5f1's 2026-09-20 unblock note and nvbr's "The blocker is VOID" section — which is why the check reads the assertion and not the contradiction: a reader meets the first paragraph first. Two blocks were real but misattributed rather than void: ktt2 waits on an independent back-translator (a capability, not a bean) and that block stands in its own §Blocked with waits-on/since/expires/handoff; rnfl's rename is not merely unblocked but MOTIVATED by what scrapped `fsch` — under the settled directory model `folio/` is a declared directory holding a `folio` graph.
